reto-md.title: reto md
description: I built the web presence for Reto MD, a mobile app that prepares Mexican physicians for the ENARM residency exam. Its websites showcase the product, sell memberships, and acquire users.

The corporate site features products, courses, events, podcasts, job listings, and a blog. I built it with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, using TanStack Query for data fetching and NextAuth with Firebase for authentication.

I consolidated the specialty websites into one multi-tenant application with App Router and next-intl. Each specialty’s branding, content, and features are configuration-driven, removing the need to duplicate projects.
I wrote the entire web codebase, owning frontend implementation, service integrations, and a shared architecture that simplifies maintenance and future launches.
reto-md.stack: Next.js · React · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS · TanStack Query · NextAuth · Firebase · next-intl · PostHog · Vercel

365-dias-de-ajedrez.title: 365 días de ajedrez
description: I turned my experience as a chess coach into a platform that brings my academy’s teaching, study, and training into one digital experience.

Powered by Next.js, React, and TypeScript, it combines courses and classes with game databases, a move trainer, puzzles, and analysis boards, with role-based access for students, instructors, and administrators.
Having student information in one place helps me spot individual learning needs and common challenges, tailor my coaching, and improve the program and learning materials.
I own the full product lifecycle, from defining requirements and designing the experience to building a platform around the way my academy works.
365-dias-de-ajedrez.stack: Figma · Next.js · React · TypeScript · Payload CMS · Prisma · PostgreSQL · Chessground · chessops · Cloudinary · Vitest · Storybook · Vercel
365-dias-de-ajedrez.imageAlt: Home page of 365 Días de Ajedrez

cuarteto-fratres.title: cuarteto fratres
description: I designed and built Cuarteto Fratres’ website to showcase their music and support bookings for concerts, weddings, and private events.

Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Payload CMS on PostgreSQL, it brings together upcoming performances, musician profiles, repertoire, and contact. The group manages content and booking inquiries independently.
I chose a single-page layout to make it easy to discover the quartet and get in touch, with a visual identity built around black-and-white photography and lime accents.
I handled the project end to end, from product planning and design to development, CMS modeling, and deployment.
cuarteto-fratres.stack: Figma · Next.js · React · TypeScript · Payload CMS · PostgreSQL · Vercel Blob · Vitest · Vercel
cuarteto-fratres.imageAlt: Home page of the Cuarteto Fratres site: headline on a dark background, portrait of the quartet and upcoming concert dates

vallarta-tours.title: vallarta tours
description: Vallarta TOURS is the fictional brand I use to showcase a website I originally built for a boat tour operator in Puerto Vallarta. The original site was live; after it was taken offline, I adapted the branding and selected content to preserve the work as a portfolio piece.

Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and next-intl, it presents five tours, experience details, a booking flow, and contact information in Spanish and English. The showcase version serves static content.

I localized page URLs alongside the content to keep navigation consistent in both languages. Switching languages takes visitors to the equivalent page, so they can continue browsing without losing their place.
I handled product planning, design in Figma, development, testing with Vitest, and deployment on Vercel.
vallarta-tours.stack: Figma · Next.js · React · TypeScript · next-intl · Vitest · Vercel
vallarta-tours.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Vallarta TOURS site

about.title: about me
about.subtitle: UI design · Frontend · Full Stack
about.quote: I don't separate the design of the interface, the code that makes it work and the decision of what is worth building.
paragraphs: I come from UI design and frontend. That is where I learned to solve the visual detail, the accessibility and the behaviour of the interface before moving towards the back end, where today I work with data, authentication and deployment.

Founding 365 Días de Ajedrez forced me to decide with judgement: what to build first, what to leave out and how to communicate it. It also put me in charge of the screen design, the web development and the advertising of the product.
I am looking for a team where I can contribute to the interface without losing sight of the whole product.
